flashcards.front: What does a position-time graph show?
flashcards.back: It shows position as a function of time, not the physical path of the object.
flashcards.explanation: The graph depicts x(t), meaning it tracks position over time, not the spatial trajectory.

flashcards.front: Can average velocity be zero if an object moved?
flashcards.back: Yes, if the object returns to its starting position, the displacement is zero.
flashcards.explanation: Average velocity is displacement over time; zero displacement results in zero average velocity.

flashcards.front: What is instantaneous velocity on a position-time graph?
flashcards.back: The slope of the tangent line to the curve at that point.
flashcards.explanation: The derivative dx/dt represents the slope of the tangent at any given time t.

flashcards.front: Why does the third derivative of position lack a name?
flashcards.back: No physical equations explicitly involve the third derivative.
flashcards.explanation: Only the first two derivatives (velocity and acceleration) are used in fundamental equations like F=ma.
